cues.en: I want to take a step back from calculus per se and talk about a quantity that I've mentioned several times already and you've probably heard before.
cues.zh: 我想先從微積分本身退一步，談一個我已經提過好幾次、你大概也聽過的量。

cues.en: It's this quantity called an infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 這個量叫作無窮小。

cues.en: But what even is an infinitesimal?
cues.zh: 不過，無窮小到底是什麼？

cues.en: Well, it turns out that infinitesimal is actually a pretty nebulous concept and a bit controversial.
cues.zh: 原來，無窮小其實是個相當模糊、也有點爭議的概念。

cues.en: Plenty of mathematicians for hundreds of years have voiced serious concerns about the existence and the applications of infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 幾百年來，許多數學家都對無窮小的存在與應用，表達過嚴重疑慮。

cues.en: And to be honest, the more you think about it, the weirder the concept becomes.
cues.zh: 老實說，你想得越多，這個概念就越奇怪。

cues.en: And then to have calculus kind of be based on this thing that's nebulous and weird and controversial is, well, it's thought provoking.
cues.zh: 而微積分竟然建立在這種模糊、奇怪又有爭議的東西上，真是很引人深思。

cues.en: Let's put it that way.
cues.zh: 就這麼說吧。

cues.en: So in this video, I want to give you a formal definition of an infinitesimal and say a few words about why it's historically been controversial.
cues.zh: 所以這支影片，我想給出無窮小的正式定義，再簡單談談它在歷史上為何有爭議。

cues.en: But the upshot is that you don't need to worry about it.
cues.zh: 不過結論是，你不需要擔心。

cues.en: You can really build all of calculus from infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 真的可以從無窮小建立整個微積分，

cues.en: And the math just works out anyway.
cues.zh: 而數學依然算得通。

cues.en: It also doesn't really matter because modern calculus is constructed from limits without the use of infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 而且這其實也沒什麼關係，因為現代微積分是從極限建立，不必使用無窮小。

cues.en: So it's not really anything to lose sleep over.
cues.zh: 所以不值得為這件事失眠。

cues.en: All right, so let's begin.
cues.zh: 好，開始吧。

cues.en: Infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 無窮小。

cues.en: What does this even mean?
cues.zh: 這到底是什麼意思？

cues.en: Well, the easiest way to think about it is that it's the opposite of infinity.
cues.zh: 最容易的想法，是把它視為無窮大的相反。

cues.en: So infinity is big.
cues.zh: 無窮大很大，

cues.en: It is bigger than the biggest thing you can possibly imagine.
cues.zh: 比你能想像最大的東西還大。

cues.en: And an infinitesimal is like the inverse of infinity.
cues.zh: 無窮小就像無窮大的倒數。

cues.en: So imagine one over infinity.
cues.zh: 想像 1 除以無窮大。

cues.en: Now there's a few different notations for the infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 無窮小有幾種不同的記號。

cues.en: Epsilon is Greek lowercase character.
cues.zh: Epsilon 是希臘小寫字母，

cues.en: Epsilon is the most common notation.
cues.zh: ε 是最常見的記號。

cues.en: And in calculus, we also use concepts like Die D, X, delta, or nebula.
cues.zh: 在微積分裡，也使用像 dy、dx、Δ 或 ∇ 這些概念。

cues.en: I'll introduce these other notations as they come up in the rest of the course.
cues.zh: 課程之後遇到這些記號時，我會再介紹。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: But what does this even mean?
cues.zh: 但這究竟是什麼意思？

cues.en: An infinitesimal is not just the smallest possible thing you can think of.
cues.zh: 無窮小不只是你能想到最小的東西。

cues.en: It's actually smaller than the smallest possible thing you can think of.
cues.zh: 它其實比你能想到最小的東西還小，

cues.en: Well, somehow still being larger than zero.
cues.zh: 卻又以某種方式仍然大於零。

cues.en: And also, like with infinity, the infinitesimal is it's not a real number.
cues.zh: 而且和無窮大一樣，無窮小不是實數。

cues.en: It doesn't exist in the real number line.
cues.zh: 它不存在於實數線上。

cues.en: You know, the line with zero in the middle and all the positive numbers to the right and the negative numbers to the left.
cues.zh: 就是中間有零、右邊全是正數、左邊全是負數的那條線。

cues.en: So Epsilon is not anywhere on this line.
cues.zh: 所以 ε 不在這條線上的任何地方，

cues.en: Just like infinity is not anywhere on this line.
cues.zh: 就像無窮大也不在這條線上的任何地方。

cues.en: So an infinitesimal is smaller than any real number.
cues.zh: 所以無窮小比任何實數都小。

cues.en: An analogy would be like fractions and integers.
cues.zh: 可以用分數和整數來類比。

cues.en: So here we have the set of all integers, and the smallest integer is one.
cues.zh: 這裡有所有整數的集合，而最小的整數是 1。

cues.en: There is no integer that is closer to zero than one.
cues.zh: 沒有整數比 1 更接近零。

cues.en: But of course we have rational numbers and one half is smaller than one.
cues.zh: 但當然，有理數裡的二分之一比 1 小。

cues.en: It's closer to zero than one.
cues.zh: 它比 1 更接近零。

cues.en: But if we are only considering the field of integers, then one half doesn't exist.
cues.zh: 不過如果只考慮整數這個數域，二分之一就不存在。

cues.en: It is not part of the integer system.
cues.zh: 它不是整數系統的一部分。

cues.en: And so it's kind of similar to an infinitesimal and real numbers.
cues.zh: 所以無窮小與實數的關係，有點類似。

cues.en: An infinitesimal is not a real number, and yet it's smaller than the smallest real number.
cues.zh: 無窮小不是實數，卻比最小的實數還小。

cues.en: And it gets even weirder because there isn't just the infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 而且還會更奇怪，因為並不只有一個無窮小。

cues.en: There are many infinitesimal, and some infinitesimal are actually bigger than other infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 有很多無窮小，有些甚至比其他無窮小更大。

cues.en: For example, you can sum to different, positive, infinitesimal to make a third infinitesimal that is somehow larger than the other two.
cues.zh: 例如，把兩個不同的正無窮小相加，可以得到第三個無窮小，而且比前兩個都大。

cues.en: And yet somehow those three infinite decimals are all smaller than the smallest possible real number.
cues.zh: 但這三個無窮小，卻又都比最小可能的實數還小。

cues.en: And furthermore, an infinitesimal squared is smaller than that infinitesimal not squared.
cues.zh: 而且，無窮小的平方，比沒有平方的那個無窮小還小。

cues.en: Honestly, though, at some point these are these are just words that I'm saying they start to lose meaning.
cues.zh: 老實說，到某個程度，這些只是我嘴裡說出的詞句，開始失去意義。

cues.en: Or at least it's hard to imagine what they really are.
cues.zh: 或至少很難想像它們真正是什麼。

cues.en: Anyway, let's have a formal definition.
cues.zh: 總之，來看正式定義。

cues.en: An infinitesimal is a number that is larger than zero, but smaller than R, where R is any real number.
cues.zh: 無窮小是一個大於零，但小於 r 的數字，而 r 是任意實數。

cues.en: So any real number you can think of even the teeniest, tiniest, tiniest, real number and something smaller than that is epsilon or infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 所以你能想到任何實數，即使再微小、再微小，都還有比它更小的 ε，也就是無窮小。

cues.en: Now, at a casual glance, this might seem fine, but from a theoretical perspective it's problematic.
cues.zh: 乍看之下可能沒問題，但理論上有問題。

cues.en: And it's problematic because there is an infinite number of real numbers.
cues.zh: 原因是，實數有無限多個。

cues.en: That is to say, you can always add an extra number between two numbers.
cues.zh: 也就是說，任意兩個數之間，總可以再加入另一個數。

cues.en: So let's consider this.
cues.zh: 所以來想想。

cues.en: Here is the real number line zoomed in and to zero and one, of course, there is a real number smaller than one.
cues.zh: 這裡把實數線放大到零和 1 之間。當然，有比 1 小的實數。

cues.en: In fact, one way to think about it is by taking the average of these two numbers.
cues.zh: 事實上，一種想法是取這兩個數的平均。

cues.en: So the average of zero and one is one half.
cues.zh: 零和 1 的平均是二分之一。

cues.en: And of course, we can get closer to zero by taking the average of zero.
cues.zh: 當然，再取零和這個數的平均，就能更接近零，

cues.en: And this number, which is a quarter and so on, unending.
cues.zh: 得到四分之一，依此類推，永不停止。

cues.en: You can always take this number and have it to get closer to zero.
cues.zh: 總可以把這個數減半，進一步接近零。

cues.en: And so where is Epsilon on this line?
cues.zh: 所以 ε 在這條線的哪裡？

cues.en: Where is our infinitesimal?
cues.zh: 我們的無窮小在哪裡？

cues.en: Well, it's not on this line, infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 它不在這條線上。無窮小，

cues.en: These are not part of the real numbers.
cues.zh: 不屬於實數。

cues.en: So we can't really include them here, just like we cannot really include one half in the set of integers, even though one half is smaller than one.
cues.zh: 所以不能真的把它們放進來，就像不能把二分之一放進整數集合，即使二分之一比 1 小。

cues.en: But who cares?
cues.zh: 但誰在乎呢？

cues.en: You know, who cares?
cues.zh: 誰在乎？

cues.en: Why is this controversial?
cues.zh: 這為什麼有爭議？

cues.en: Well, mixing different fields so integers and real numbers and real numbers and infinitesimal was historically kind of difficult.
cues.zh: 歷史上，混用不同數域，例如整數與實數、實數與無窮小，有點困難。

cues.en: Mathematicians didn't like the idea of using non-real numbers to develop calculus with real numbers.
cues.zh: 數學家不喜歡用非實數，來發展以實數運作的微積分。

cues.en: And actually, this concern has decreased in recent mathematical history because it's been shown that
cues.zh: 不過在近代數學史裡，這個疑慮已經減少，因為已證明

cues.en: infinitesimal can actually rigorously correspond to a real quantity, and we don't need to just use them heuristics as they were first used by Leibniz and Newton.
cues.zh: 無窮小可以嚴謹地對應實際的量，不必像萊布尼茲與牛頓最早使用時那樣，只靠啟發式的想法。

cues.en: Well, another part of the problem is that the concept of infinitesimal always has some tiny errors, some little bits of leftover.
cues.zh: 另一部分問題是，無窮小的概念總是會有一些微小誤差、一點點剩餘。

cues.en: And the reason is that if you have two points on a curve, then there's always going to be some little tiny piece of curve that's still bent, that's still left over.
cues.zh: 原因是，如果曲線上有兩個點，總有一小段曲線仍然彎著、還留在那裡，

cues.en: If you draw a straight line between these two points, even if these two points are infinitesimally
cues.zh: 即使兩點無窮接近，在它們之間

cues.en: close now, this little error, this concept of having a small error here will be even more clear when you learn about integration, for example, with Riemann sums.
cues.zh: 畫一條直線也是如此。這個微小誤差的概念，等學到積分，例如黎曼和時，會更清楚。

cues.en: So no matter how much you zoom in, there's always the risk of these two points, not completely capturing this little piece of curvature here.
cues.zh: 所以不管放大多少，兩點始終可能無法完全捕捉這裡的小段彎曲。

cues.en: Now, on the other hand, if the infinitesimal are so close that they are smaller than the change in
cues.zh: 但另一方面，如果無窮小接近到，比函數的 x 變化量

cues.en: X or the change in Y of the function, then there actually is no change in the function and therefore there is no slope between those two points.
cues.zh: 或 y 變化量還小，那麼函數其實就沒有變化，因此兩點之間沒有斜率。

cues.en: But do we do we actually even use infinitesimal?
cues.zh: 但我們到底有沒有真的使用無窮小？

cues.en: Well, yes and no.
cues.zh: 有，也沒有。

cues.en: Calculus was originally developed using infinitesimal by Leibniz and Newton, but a lot of other mathematicians
cues.zh: 微積分最初是萊布尼茲與牛頓用無窮小發展出來的，但當時很多其他數學家

cues.en: at the time didn't like it, and eventually re derived calculus using limits.
cues.zh: 不喜歡，最後改用數值趨近零時的極限，重新推導微積分。

cues.en: As numbers go to zero, of course, you're now familiar with limits and in the next section of the course
cues.zh: 當然，你現在已經熟悉極限，而課程下一節，

cues.en: you will see how to use limits to compute the derivatives of functions.
cues.zh: 會看到如何用極限計算函數的導數。

cues.en: That's how calculus is developed and that's how it's taught and used.
cues.zh: 這就是現在微積分建立、教授和使用的方式。

cues.en: Now, although we actually still invoke the concept of infinitesimal when it's convenient to help us understand or work with differential calculus.
cues.zh: 雖然實際上，當有助於理解或使用微分學時，我們仍然會援用無窮小的概念。

cues.en: Now, this is a slide from the next section, So you haven't seen this slide yet.
cues.zh: 這是下一節的投影片，所以你還沒看過。

cues.en: And don't worry, if you don't really understand what this stuff means, you'll learn in the next section.
cues.zh: 如果現在不太懂這些意思，別擔心，下一節就會學。

cues.en: But just to foreshadow that, a derivative is basically the slope of a function.
cues.zh: 不過先預告一下，導數基本上就是函數的斜率。

cues.en: It's the change in the function with an infinitesimal change in x.
cues.zh: 是 x 有無窮小變化時，函數的變化。

cues.en: So the point is that in practice, in modern calculus, we actually build up the principles of modern calculus from limits and not from infinitesimal.
cues.zh: 所以重點是，在現代微積分的實務中，我們其實從極限，而非無窮小，建立現代微積分的原理。

cues.en: But you actually can still use real infinitesimal in calculus.
cues.zh: 不過，確實仍然可以在微積分裡使用真正的無窮小。

cues.en: That's called nonstandard calculus.
cues.zh: 這叫作非標準微積分。

cues.en: And I'm not going to discuss it any further, but if you're curious, you can look it up, you can read about it online on Wikipedia, for example, you can watch videos about it on YouTube.
cues.zh: 我不會繼續討論，不過有興趣可以查資料，例如維基百科上的文章，或 YouTube 上的影片。

cues.en: So the point is, most mathematicians and basically all engineers and data scientists and anyone else
cues.zh: 所以重點是，大多數數學家，基本上所有工程師、資料科學家，以及其他

cues.en: using applied calculus, they say, well, you know, infinitesimal are useful to think about.
cues.zh: 應用微積分的人，都會說，無窮小是個有用的思考方式。

cues.en: They help us with the concepts of calculus.
cues.zh: 它們能幫助理解微積分的概念。

cues.en: So let's just ignore all of this philosophical and historical annoyances because, yeah, everything just works when you use these things.
cues.zh: 所以先忽略這些哲學和歷史上的麻煩吧，因為使用它們時，一切確實都算得通。

cues.en: And actually if you are.
cues.zh: 其實，如果你

cues.en: Thinking about computer science, then the idea of an infinitesimal is actually not so weird.
cues.zh: 從電腦科學的角度思考，無窮小的想法也沒有那麼奇怪。

cues.en: You know, computers cannot represent arbitrarily small numbers.
cues.zh: 電腦無法表示任意小的數字。

cues.en: Computers can only approximate certain mathematical functions, for example, irrational numbers.
cues.zh: 電腦只能近似某些數學函數，例如無理數。

cues.en: There's always going to be some truncation, some precision error in the approximation of a number.
cues.zh: 數字的近似總會有截斷、精度誤差。

cues.en: And of course, this is something that I have discussed many, many times in the difference between using numpy and sim pi.
cues.zh: 當然，我已經在 NumPy 和 SymPy 的差異中，討論過很多很多次。

cues.en: And so on computers, there's something called EPS or epsilon, which on modern computers is somewhere around ten to the -16.
cues.zh: 所以電腦裡有個叫 eps，或 epsilon 的東西，在現代電腦上，大約是十的負 16 次方。

cues.en: That's the smallest number that programs like Python can really represent.
cues.zh: 那是 Python 這類程式真正能表示的最小數字。

cues.en: Well, let me let me rephrase that to be a little bit more precise.
cues.zh: 不過，讓我重新說得更精確一點。

cues.en: The machine epsilon is the smallest distance between two successive numbers, generally the number one and the next larger number.
cues.zh: 機器 epsilon，是相鄰兩個數字之間最小的距離，通常指 1 和下一個更大的數字。

cues.en: So if you have a computer science background, then maybe it helps to think about an infinitesimal as being any number that is smaller than the machine precision.
cues.zh: 所以如果你有電腦科學背景，把無窮小想成任何小於機器精度的數字，也許有幫助。

cues.en: And just to be clear, this is just an analogy to help you think about the concept.
cues.zh: 說清楚一點，這只是幫助你思考這個概念的類比。

cues.en: Don't don't take this statement too literally.
cues.zh: 不要太過照字面解讀。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: Anyway, there's a lot more that could be said about infinitesimal limits and the history of calculus.
cues.zh: 總之，關於無窮小、極限，以及微積分的歷史，還有很多可以談。

cues.en: And, you know, many topics in math become kind of philosophical when you start to dig into them.
cues.zh: 深入探究時，數學裡很多主題都會變得有點哲學性。

cues.en: And Infinitesimal are a great example of the intersection between mathematics and philosophy.
cues.zh: 無窮小就是數學與哲學交會的一個好例子。

cues.en: Well, anyway, I hope you found this video to be thought provoking and enjoyable.
cues.zh: 總之，希望你覺得這支影片引人深思，也看得愉快。

cues.en: And now back to our regularly scheduled programming.
cues.zh: 現在回到我們原訂的節目。
